name: chocolate-doom
why: An accurate Doom source port; a classic game, but the strangeness is in its historical fidelity rather than the terminal.

brief.what_it_is: Chocolate Doom is a source port of Doom, the 1993 id Software shooter, that runs on modern computers. It takes an original Doom game data file (an IWAD, which you must supply yourself) and runs the game with display and input meant to feel like the DOS original. The package also ships ports of Heretic, Hexen and Strife on the same engine, plus setup tools and a server executable. The brew formula installs the engine only, with no levels included.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the project aims to accurately reproduce the original DOS version of Doom and other games based on the Doom engine in a form that can be run on modern computers. Its stated aims include staying 100% free and open source, accurate reproduction 'including bugs', and compatibility with DOS demo, configuration and savegame files.
brief.how_it_works: The README describes a faithful reimplementation rather than an emulator: it aims to match the DOS executables' behaviour, including the original bugs, which are kept on purpose and documented in a NOT-BUGS file. For total conversions, the '-merge' option merges a PWAD into the main IWAD in memory, so the IWAD on disk is not modified. Settings live in a chocolate-doom.cfg file alongside compatibility with the DOS default.cfg.

commands_seen.context: README example for playing a total conversion: '-merge' simulates the DEUSF merge in memory instead of modifying the IWAD on disk.
README example for Batman Doom, adding a DeHackEd patch with -deh after the merged WAD. The README labels this line 'Batman Doom'.
README example for Army of Darkness Doom, merging the WAD and applying a DeHackEd patch.

brief.install_notes: The brew formula installs only the engine and no levels. You need your own original Doom IWAD (the brew caveat says you can copy over levels you already own, and points to free levels online). Setup is done with the chocolate-setup tools (chocolate-doom-setup and the Heretic, Hexen and Strife equivalents) to edit chocolate-doom.cfg, and the README says DOS default.cfg files should work unchanged. The README points to an INSTALL file for play setup and a CMDLINE file for binary distributions; I did not read those.
brief.standout: Its fidelity is the point: it deliberately keeps Vanilla Doom bugs and aims to match DOS behaviour on display and input. The '-merge' option lets total conversions run without the DEUSF merge step that the DOS versions required, by merging the WAD directory in memory.
brief.status: Unknown as to a current release, though the project describes itself as under continual active development. The homepage I read is a cached MediaWiki page last edited 18 January 2019, so its content may be dated. The GitHub README is current in form and points to a live issue tracker, but I saw no release date or last-commit date.
brief.caveats: No game levels are included; the original Doom data files are still under copyright, so you must supply your own or find free levels. The README says the port is not perfect and some DOS behaviour is very hard to reproduce. Music playback has several options, described in a separate README.Music file. Licensed under the GNU GPL. The homepage also mentions Crispy Doom, a friendly fork with extra features.
quotes: Chocolate Doom aims to accurately reproduce the original DOS version of Doom and other games based on the Doom engine in a form that can be run on modern computers.
Accurate reproduction of the original DOS versions of the games, including bugs.
Chocolate Doom is not perfect. Although it aims to accurately emulate and reproduce the DOS executables, some behavior can be very difficult to reproduce.
